metadata.name: Influenza & Pneumonia (10-year)
metadata.description: 10-year risk of death from influenza and pneumonia, primarily affecting elderly and immunocompromised individuals

curves.source: Derived from the unstratified curve using the male:female influenza/pneumonia mortality ratio ~1.35 (CDC WONDER via American Lung Association Trends in Pneumonia and Influenza Mortality: age-adjusted 2013 male 18.6 vs female 13.9 per 100k; MMWR 2020;69(40) QuickStats confirms higher male rates in every 65+ age group)
curves.notes: male = 1.15x combined, female = 0.85x combined (equal population shares)

riskFactors.name: Flu Vaccination (Current Year)
riskFactors.notes: Vaccine effectiveness ~40-60% against mortality; varies by season and strain match

mapping.notes: Flu vaccine reduces mortality risk by ~40-60%

riskFactors.name: Pneumococcal Vaccination
riskFactors.citation: Kim S, et al. Prior pneumococcal vaccination improves in-hospital mortality among elderly hospitalized with community-acquired pneumonia. BMC Pulm Med. 2024;24:168
riskFactors.notes: 30-day mortality aHR 0.576 (0.409-0.812) in vaccinated CAP patients >=65. Conditional on hospitalization (case-fatality effect); population-level prevention benefit is smaller.

riskFactors.name: Immunocompromised Status
riskFactors.citation: Wang L, et al. The severity and risk factors for mortality in immunocompromised adult patients hospitalized with influenza-related pneumonia. Ann Clin Microbiol Antimicrob. 2021;20:60
riskFactors.notes: 30-day mortality OR 3.206 (1.926-5.335) for immunocompromised vs immunocompetent influenza pneumonia.

riskFactors.name: Chronic Lung Disease (COPD)
riskFactors.citation: Barker WH, Mullooly JP. Pneumonia and influenza deaths during epidemics: implications for prevention. Arch Intern Med. 1982;142(1):85-89 (PMID 7053739)
riskFactors.notes: Epidemic P&I death rates <10/100k in healthy adults vs >600/100k in chronically ill (870/100k with combined cardiopulmonary disease). Effect driven by higher infection/pneumonia incidence (RR 1.36) more than case fatality (aHR 1.12, ns, Miyashita 2021).

riskFactors.name: Diabetes
riskFactors.citation: Miyashita K, Nakatani E, Hozumi H, et al. Risk Factors for Pneumonia and Death in Adult Patients With Seasonal Influenza: A Population-Based Study. Open Forum Infect Dis. 2021;8(3):ofab068
riskFactors.notes: Diabetes: 28-day mortality HR 1.69 (1.10-2.60), pneumonia incidence RR 1.56 (1.25-1.94); all-infection mortality HR 1.82 (1.78-1.86) in T2D (Carey 2024).

riskFactors.name: Heart Disease
riskFactors.citation: Miyashita K, Nakatani E, Hozumi H, et al. Open Forum Infect Dis. 2021;8(3):ofab068
riskFactors.notes: Congestive heart failure: 28-day mortality HR 2.11 (1.49-2.98); evidence is CHF-specific — may overstate stable coronary disease.

riskFactors.name: Annual Influenza Vaccination
riskFactors.citation: Gross PA, Hermogenes AW, Sacks HS, Lau J, Levandowski RA. The efficacy of influenza vaccine in elderly persons. A meta-analysis and review of the literature. Ann Intern Med. 1995;123(7):518-527
riskFactors.notes: Pooled cohort estimates: 68% (56-76%) reduction in influenza-associated death and ~50% in pneumonia/influenza hospitalization among vaccinated elderly. Modeled conservatively at HR 0.5 because healthy-vaccinee bias inflates observational estimates and the model outcome includes non-influenza pneumonia.
